[Carol]: Your earlier suggestions were great, thank you — they made me realize how ad hoc my current setup is. I’m a freelance designer usually juggling 5–10 client projects, plus admin work (quotes, invoices, email) and personal learning like courses. At the moment I just throw everything into one big task list and dip into the app whenever I feel behind, which means I don’t have a steady daily or weekly rhythm. Could you walk me through a simple, concrete template in the app for someone in my situation: how you’d structure areas/projects and tags, and exactly what you’d recommend I review in a quick morning check‑in and an end‑of‑day wrap‑up so it becomes a real habit?
rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Planning daily check-ins**

I'm thinking about my morning check-in steps, like reviewing my inbox and filtering tasks tagged #next or due today by priority. I want to pick the top 3 tasks for work across clients and also check meetings and any timers or waiting items. For my end-of-day wrap-up, I should quickly complete tasks, capture new tasks in my inbox, set priorities for the next day, and log my time and progress. I’m inviting feedback to tailor this process!
rounds.response: Great — here’s a compact, concrete template you can set up in minutes: Areas = Clients, Admin, Learning, Personal, plus a top-level Inbox for quick capture; inside Clients create one Project per client (and sub-projects per engagement if needed), Admin has Projects like Quotes, Invoices, Email, and Learning has one Project per course or curriculum. Use tags for quick filtering: #next (ready to work), #waiting (blocked/by others), #urgent, #someday, #client-[name], and optional time tags like @15m/@1h; use priority stars or flags for immediate focus. Morning check‑in (5–10 min): empty Inbox into Projects/tags, open a Today view showing tasks due or tagged #next, pick your top 3 client tasks for the day, confirm meetings and any #waiting items to follow up on. End‑of‑day (5 min): mark progress/complete small wins, capture loose notes into Inbox, set 1–3 top #next tasks for tomorrow, and archive or update any finished project statuses — tell me a typical workday and I’ll adapt this into a ready-to-use template for you.
